description:
FILED s539c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-15), the residue of #4761 (PPI §65, group BA: the keep_line_endings attribute; PCL: _file_line_endings / _eval_heredoc_line_endings).

perl 5.40.3, an eval STRING (one buffer; the bytes built at run time):

    my $c = "my \$v = <<\"T\";\nx\r\r\ny\r\r\nT\r\r\n\$v";  print unpack("H*", eval $c);   # 780a0a790a0a  (each CR a line end)
    my $c = "my \$v = <<\"T\";\nx\ry\rT\r\n\$v";             print unpack("H*", eval $c);   # 780a790a      (lone CR line ends)

PPI with keep_line_endings splits lines at LF only, so a here-doc whose lines end in a lone CR (or CR CR LF) finds no terminator line.  s539c gives such an eval text (a lone CR somewhere AND an unterminated here-doc, Pl::Parser::_lone_cr_heredoc_unterminated) PPI's old normalised reading (_normalised_line_endings: CR CR LF / CR LF / lone CR -> LF) -- what the base did: the lone-CR shape reads like perl (780a790a), the CR CR LF shape reads 780a790a where perl reads 780a0a790a0a (a pre-existing difference, the base reads the same), and every CR of a STRING in that eval text is lost (as on the base).

Probe rows: scratch/s539c/p/cr/e-heredoc-crcrlf.pl, e-heredocq-crcrlf.pl (DIFF, = base), e-heredoc-cr.pl, e-heredocq-cr.pl (SAME) -- worktree agent-ade4d9bd1dff36571.

FIX SHAPE if it is ever worth it: the here-doc reader is the one place that knows where the body starts; perl's eval reading is "within the here-doc scan, each CR LF and each lone CR is a line end".  A PPI attribute value (keep_line_endings => 'eval'?) would encode perl's eval rule inside PPI -- discuss before building.  No real program in the corpora or the board holds either shape (2 of 2,158 files hold any CR at all).
subject: PCL eval mode: an eval STRING whose here-doc lines end in a lone CR or CR CR LF -- perl's eval reads each CR as a line end there (CR CR LF -> two LFs); PCL takes PPI's old normalised reading for such a text (string CRs lost, CR CR LF -> one LF) (#4761 residue)
triage_reason: rare: an eval string whose here-doc lines end in a lone CR
